label: Nebulae
description: A separately loaded, hand-curated overlay of the catalogued nebulae within about 500 ly, plus the Orion Nebula, rendered as approximate 3D volumes.

sources.name: Kounkel et al. (2017); VLBA distance to the Orion Nebula Cluster
O'Dell (2001); structure of the Orion Nebula
Alfonso & García-Varela (2023); Gaia astrometric distance to the Pleiades
Gibson & Nordsieck (2003); Pleiades reflection nebula scattering geometry
van den Bergh (1966); Catalogue of Reflection Nebulae (VizieR VII/21)
Lynds (1965); Catalogue of Bright Nebulae (VizieR VII/9)
Sharpless (1959); Catalogue of H II Regions (VizieR VII/20)
Magakian (2003); merged catalogue of reflection nebulae (southern completeness check)
Chornay & Walton (2021); Gaia EDR3 planetary nebula central stars with HASH radii
Frew & Parker (2010); planetary nebula mimics including Abell 35
Gaia Collaboration (2021); Gaia EDR3 parallaxes (VizieR I/350)
van Leeuwen (2007); Hipparcos new reduction parallaxes (VizieR I/311)

cutoffPolicy: Every reflection nebula, H II region and planetary nebula that is listed in NGC/IC, van den Bergh, Sharpless or HASH, spans at least 5 arcmin, and whose adopted distance is within 1 sigma of 500 ly (distance - error <= 153.3 pc). Distances come from the SIMBAD-adopted parallax (Gaia EDR3, else Hipparcos 2007) of the illuminating or central star; several stars use an inverse-variance mean. Sizes come from LBN for named NGC/IC nebulae, Sharpless or HASH for ionized nebulae, and twice the van den Bergh maximum radius otherwise. The Orion Nebula (about 1265 ly) is kept as a showcase beyond the cutoff. Excluded: dark nebulae and molecular clouds, nebulae under 5 arcmin (most young-star nebulae in Taurus, Ophiuchus and Corona Australis), the Corona Australis nebulae NGC 6726/6727 and IC 4812 (illuminating stars at 155 pc), the possible planetary nebula FP J1912-0331, and H-alpha-only ionized regions such as Spica's.
